stem: Which stain is used to help diagnose Hirschsprung disease by assessing for normal bowel innervation?
explanation: Calretinin staining is used in Hirschsprung disease to highlight normal enteric innervation, with loss of staining in aganglionic bowel.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because Gram stain is used to identify bacteria, not to assess enteric ganglion cells.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because calretinin staining is positive in normal bowel but absent in the aganglionic segments of Hirschsprung disease.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because haemotoxylin and eosin is a routine histological stain, but calretinin is the more specific stain used to assess enteric innervation in Hirschsprung disease.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because Sudan black stains lipids and is not used to identify the enteric nervous system.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because Ziehl-Neelsen stain is used for acid-fast organisms, not for diagnosing Hirschsprung disease.

source.hint: This specific immunohistochemical marker helps pathologists visualize the health of the enteric nervous system.
